This folder holds the combined result of several mods changing the same script.
      It must load before all mods, otherwise the original files overwrite the merge —
      the game then fails with “Could not find function ...”, and the error only points at the source mods, hiding the real cause.
      This panel is display-only; enabling, disabling and ordering are up to the buttons below.

conf.anno_replace_detail: {names} both use @replaceMethod to replace functions like {fn} wholesale. The game keeps only the copy that loads last — the other one's changes (including logic it wraps elsewhere) disappear without any error. These cannot be merged automatically: either change the load order to decide which one wins, or ask the author to switch to @wrapMethod.{more}
conf.anno_wrap_detail: {names} each attach their own code around functions like {fn}. This is a stacking mechanism meant to coexist and is not a problem by itself — but the stacking order follows the load order, so if a feature behaves differently after you reordered mods, check back against this list.{more}

conf.anno_wrap_one: {n} function has extra logic from {m} mods
conf.bundle_data_detail: {names} both contain {head}{more} in their bundles. These are item/stat definitions — again only one copy takes effect, and the other side's changes silently stop working.
conf.bundle_data_many: {n} definition files are provided by {m} mods at once
conf.bundle_data_one: {n} definition file is provided by {m} mods at once
conf.bundle_ui_detail: {names} both contain {what} in their bundles. The game loads only one copy, and the other mod's UI changes disappear wholesale — the typical symptom is “the feature works, but the UI looks wrong or is missing”. These assets cannot be merged the way scripts can. Do not rush to uninstall: sometimes the upstream mod has already absorbed the other's changes, so judge by the actual result.

conf.bundle_ui_one: {n} UI file is provided by {m} mods at once

conf.w3_stale_detail: The game itself is v{base}, and {pairs} use older tables. The game cannot read text added by those tables, so those spots show ## or blank in the UI — the feature usually still works, only the text is missing (for example, a box that should appear does not). This comes from old packing tools on the author's side; the only fix is a mod update.

conf.ws_encoding_detail: {names} contains {enc}-encoded scripts. The 5.00 build only reads UTF-8 — these files are read as garbage, the whole script fails to compile, and the game greets you with a wall of red errors. These are old 4.x-era packages; the author needs to re-export them with current tools, and re-encoding them yourself may not save them.

localize.loading_panel: Checking the language table of each mod…
localize.run_none: No menu text here needs translating
localize.run_note: About {n} seconds · you see the result first; nothing is written until you confirm
localize.run_sub: Each source string is translated once. Results wait here until you decide to write them.
localize.stale_title: This English was the name shown in the menu; Chinese in the XML has replaced it, so it never reaches the screen
localize.tip_bad: The rows in orange have translations longer than the original, so they cannot be written. Shorten them on the right — they become writable at once. You can also leave them and write the rest.
localize.why_length: Length limit: writing keeps the file size unchanged, so a translation cannot be longer than the original. Anything that does not fit is shortened automatically; what still does not fit is flagged for you to shorten — never truncated, because truncation garbles the whole screen.
localize.why_manual: Handled by menu XML: some localizations edit the menu XML directly (writing Chinese into displayName), so the menu is already Chinese. The English left in the language table is the old text that was replaced, marked as outdated — translating it again changes nothing on screen.
localize.why_names_only: Only mod and item names left; skipped by default
localize.why_script: Text lives in a script: mods such as AutoLoot put menu text straight into .ws and return it per language, so an empty language table is normal and the game displays it correctly. The app only detects this; it never edits scripts.
localize.why_unreadable: Source unreadable: the language table is encrypted and the app does not guess keys. This only means it cannot be read here — it does not mean the game has no Chinese. Do not change anything just because a mod shows up in this list.
localize.write_note: Originals are backed up automatically before writing; if anything goes wrong, use Restore original.

The order has changed and is not saved yet.

If you close now these changes are lost — press Cancel and then Save order.

order.hint_html:
Mods higher up load first; when two mods ship the same file, the one higher up (lower number) wins. To give a mod the final say, drag it up. Drag rows, or use ↑ ↓, then press Save order — the numbers 10, 20, 30… are written to mods.settings, which is the game's load priority.
Only the {on} enabled mods actually affect each other; where a disabled mod sits makes no difference. This list shows the real order (disabled rows are not hidden) — the main screen's All mods list only puts disabled mods last for readability and does not change the numbers here.
order.hint_merge: Merged files (the ones produced by Script Merger) are pinned to the very top and do not take part in this ordering — placing them second would invalidate the merge.
order.state_clean: Changes take effect only after Save order
order.state_dirty: Changes are not saved — closing now loses them

srv.need_admin: Permission denied: the game folder (or target folder) is not writable by the current user. If the game lives under Program Files, close this app and run it as administrator.
srv.not_game_root: That's not the game folder (no bin folder inside).
srv.only_nexus_links: Only Nexus links can be opened.
srv.pick_mods_first: Pick the mods to localize first.
srv.pick_unavailable: This PC can't open the picker (system dialog component unavailable). Paste the path into the field instead.
stor.archives_desc: Copies saved by the pre-1.2.4 “keep a copy of the original archive after install” feature. That feature is gone; this is only for cleaning up files it left behind — deleting them does not affect installed mods.
stor.archives_title: Original archive copies left by older versions
stor.dead_desc: Caches and logs left by early versions that are never read anymore. Keeping them only wastes space.
stor.jobs_desc: To-translate lists exported for AI and the results imported back. Finished batches can be cleared without affecting strings already written into the game or saved. The CN naming feature was retired in 1.2.5, and the old data in names.json / names/ can be cleared along with it.
stor.jobs_title: CN localization work files (incl. legacy CN naming data)
stor.localize_backups_desc: Backups left behind when version 1.1 or earlier exported to-translate lists. Newer versions keep the originals elsewhere, protected under “CN localization originals” — clearing this item does not affect restore.
stor.nexus_desc: Cached author, description and latest version info (one small file per mod). Deleting them affects nothing; the next time the app opens it queries Nexus again (only mods with an ID).
stor.other_desc: Things in the data folder that do not belong to any category above. The program never touches them; if you do not recognize where they came from, take a look in the data folder directly.
stor.quarantine_desc: Uninstalled mods are not really deleted but moved here in case you change your mind. Once you are sure, they can be deleted permanently. After that the mod files are gone for good.
stor.snapshots_desc: Before each change to mods.settings or menu files, a copy of the original is saved. These back the Undo feature — once cleared, earlier operations can no longer be undone. The program automatically keeps only the most recent 30.
stor.thumbs_desc: The covers shown on cards. Deleting them affects nothing except that cards fall back to a plain background; ones with a Nexus ID are fetched again automatically the next time the app opens, and ones without an ID can be re-imported from your old data in Settings.
stor.webview_desc: Temporary files left by the browser engine behind the UI window. Deleting them is harmless — they are rebuilt on the next start (UI preferences reset once).
track.ahead_note: The local version number is higher than the one recorded on Nexus. The two numbers usually come from different places (archive filename, old manager record, or the number the author typed on the page), so it does not mean you have a future version.
track.all_fresh: All metadata is up to date; nothing to fetch
track.busy_fetch: Contacting Nexus for metadata, one moment…
track.guess_hint_both: · Matches both locally and on Nexus
track.guess_hint_local: · This archive is in your downloads folder
track.hint_column: The Nexus column shows the version of the mod's main file, not the number the author typed on the page — the latter often lags behind the file they uploaded. Metadata is refreshed every 7 days; the just fetched tag marks a live request made now, while earlier records is a number stored before.
track.ignore_off_title: Start reminding me about this one again
track.ignore_on_title: Self-made or ported mods are not on Nexus; once marked, this one is no longer reported
track.ignored_note: Marked as not on Nexus. No longer reported.
track.missing_footer: For mods without an ID the app tries to work it out first: if the original archive is still in your downloads folder, or the mod was installed with this app before, it can be matched for you. The ones it cannot place are listed below under Possibly — pick one and version, cover and author will then update automatically.
track.muted_done: OK, this one will not be reported again
track.need_id: Enter a Nexus ID or page URL
track.nothing_missing_many: Nothing to check: {n} mods still have no Nexus ID. Use the Missing ID filter above to link them
track.nothing_missing_one: Nothing to check: {n} mod still has no Nexus ID. Use the Missing ID filter above to link it
track.page_version_hint: The Nexus page shows {v} at the top, which is the display value the author typed in; this column uses the version of the file they uploaded
track.refreshed_covers_many: Metadata updated for {n} mods, {m} covers downloaded
track.refreshed_covers_one: Metadata updated for {n} mod, {m} covers downloaded
trk.ref_bad_number: This number does not look like a Nexus ID (usually 3–6 digits)
trk.ref_not_found: No Nexus ID could be found in this text
ui.batch_title: Select several mods and enable or disable them together
ui.details_empty: Pick a mod to see its details
ui.nexus_title: Open The Witcher 3 on Nexus Mods in your browser
ui.pick_hint: Click a card to select or deselect it
ui.search_ph: Search mods, authors or Nexus ID
ui.sort_title: Only changes the order shown here — use Load order on the left to change the game's load order
ui.upd_ignore: Ignore this batch — remind me when something new shows up
ui.upd_pill_title: See which mods have new versions
upd.feed_bad_json: The update feed returned something that is not JSON
upd.feed_no_version: The update feed contains no version number
upd.feed_not_found: No released version yet — the first Release has not been published. Check again later.
upd.no_feed: Update checks are off (update_check is false in config.json). Remove that line to turn them back on.
ws.encrypted: No readable text found; this file is encrypted and cannot be edited
ws.length_changed: Internal error: the file length changed after replacement; the write was aborted (the file was not modified)
ws.not_w3strings: Not a .w3strings file (missing the RTSW header)
ws.too_few: Too little readable content; the file is treated as encrypted (it can only be translated if the author provides a CSV)
ws.unsafe: This file cannot be safely modified: {reason}
